148                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Provides 'R' bindings to the 'GGML' tensor library for machine\n    learning, optimized for 'Vulkan' GPU acceleration with a transparent CPU\n    fallback. The package features a 'Keras'-like sequential API and a\n    'PyTorch'-style 'autograd' engine for building, training, and deploying\n    neural networks. Key capabilities include high-performance 5D tensor\n    operations, 'f16' precision, and efficient quantization. It supports\n    native 'ONNX' model import (50+ operators) and 'GGUF' weight loading\n    from the 'llama.cpp' and 'Hugging Face' ecosystems. Designed for\n    zero-overhead inference via dedicated weight buffering, it integrates\n    seamlessly as a 'parsnip' engine for 'tidymodels' and provides\n    first-class learners for the 'mlr3' framework.\n    See <https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml> for more information about the\n    underlying library.
149                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Implements the generalized Gauss Markov regression, this is useful when both predictor and response have uncertainty attached to them and also when covariance within the predictor, within the response and between the predictor and the response is present. Base on the results published in guide ISO/TS 28037 (2010) <https://www.iso.org/standard/44473.html>. 
150                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Facilitates efficient visualization of Relative Synonymous Codon Usage patterns across species. Based on analytical outputs from 'codonW', 'MEGA', and 'Phylosuite', it supports multi-species 'RSCU' comparisons and allows users to explore visual analysis of structurally similar datasets.
151                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A 'grammar of graphics' approach for visualizing summary statistics from multiple Genome-wide Association Studies (GWAS). It offers geneticists, bioinformaticians, and researchers a powerful yet flexible tool for illustrating complex genetic associations using data from various GWAS datasets. The visualizations can be extensively customized, facilitating detailed comparative analysis across different genetic studies. Reference: Uffelmann, E. et al. (2021) <doi:10.1038/s43586-021-00056-9>.
152                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Create plots that combine a phylogeny and frequency dynamics.\n    Phylogenetic input can be a generic adjacency matrix or a tree of class "phylo".\n    Inspired by similar plots in publications of the labs of RE Lenski and JE\n    Barrick. Named for HJ Muller (who popularised such plots) and H Wickham (whose\n    code this package exploits).
153                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            It provides materials (i.e. 'serial axes' objects, Andrew's plot, various glyphs for scatter plot) to visualize high dimensional data. 
154                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Geometries to plot network objects with 'ggplot2'.
155                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Use multiple fill and colour scales in 'ggplot2'.
156                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Uses 'ggplot2' to create normally distributed violin plots\n    with specified means and standard deviations. This function can be\n    useful in showing hypothetically normal distributions and confidence\n    intervals.
157                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Allows plotting data on bathymetric maps using 'ggplot2'. Plotting\n  oceanographic spatial data is made as simple as feasible, but also flexible\n  for custom modifications. Data that contain geographic information from \n  anywhere around the globe can be plotted on maps generated by the basemap()\n  or qmap() functions using 'ggplot2' layers separated by the '+' operator. The \n  package uses spatial shape- ('sf') and raster ('stars') files, geospatial \n  packages for R to manipulate, and the 'ggplot2' package to plot these \n  files. The package ships with low-resolution spatial data files and \n  higher resolution files for detailed maps are stored in the \n  'ggOceanMapsLargeData' repository on GitHub and downloaded automatically \n  when needed. 
158                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Discrete scales for the colorblind-friendly 'Okabe-Ito'\n    palette, including 'color', 'fill', and 'edge_colour'. 'ggokabeito'\n    provides 'ggplot2' and 'ggraph' scales to easily use the 'Okabe-Ito'\n    palette in your data visualizations.
159                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The 'vegan' package includes several functions for adding features\n  to ordination plots: ordiarrows(),  ordiellipse(), ordihull(),\n  ordispider() and ordisurf(). This package adds these same   features to \n  ordination plots made with 'ggplot2'. In addition, gg_ordibubble() sizes\n  points relative to the value of an environmental variable. 
160                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   \n    Create groups of 'ggplot2' layers that can be easily migrated from one plot\n    to another, reducing redundant code and improving the ability to format many\n    plots that draw from the same source 'ggpacket' layers.
161                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Facilitates the creation of page layout\n    visualizations in which words are represented as rectangles with sizes\n    relating to the length of the words. Which then is divided in lines\n    and pages for easy overview of up to quite large texts.
162                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Extends 'ggplot2' functionality to the 'partykit' package. 'ggparty' provides the necessary tools to create clearly structured and highly customizable visualizations for tree-objects of the class 'party'.
163                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           A 'ggplot2' extension that enables robust image grobs in\n    panels and theme elements.
164                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Provides 'ggplot2' geoms filled with various patterns.  Includes a patterned version of every 'ggplot2' geom that has a region that can be filled with a pattern.  Provides a suite of 'ggplot2' aesthetics and scales for controlling pattern appearances.  Supports over a dozen builtin patterns (every pattern implemented by 'gridpattern') as well as allowing custom user-defined patterns.
165                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Provides tools for creating publication-ready dimensionality reduction plots, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP). This package helps visualize high-dimensional data with options for custom labels, density plots, and faceting, using the 'ggplot2' framework Wickham (2016) <doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4>.
166                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Modern Parallel Coordinate Plots have been introduced in the 1980s as \n    a way to visualize arbitrarily many numeric variables. This Grammar of Graphics implementation\n    also incorporates categorical variables into the plots in a principled manner. \n    By separating the data managing part from the visual rendering, we give full access\n    to the users while keeping the number of parameters manageably low.  
167                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Provides plotting functions for visualizing pedigrees and family trees. The package complements a behavior genetics package 'BGmisc' [Garrison et al. (2024) <doi:10.21105/joss.06203>] by rendering pedigrees using the 'ggplot2' framework. Features include support for duplicated individuals, complex mating structures, integration with simulated pedigrees, and layout customization. Due to the impending deprecation of kinship2, version 1.0 incorporates the layout helper functions from kinship2. The pedigree alignment algorithms are adapted from 'kinship2' [Sinnwell et al. (2014) <doi:10.1159/000363105>]. We gratefully acknowledge the original authors: Jason Sinnwell, Terry Therneau, Daniel Schaid, and Elizabeth Atkinson for their foundational work. 
168                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Implements methods to plot periodic data in any arbitrary range on the fly.
169                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Provides a convenient way to analyze and visualize 'PICRUSt2' output with pre-defined plots and functions. Allows for generating statistical plots about microbiome functional predictions and offers customization options. Features a one-click option for creating publication-level plots, saving time and effort in producing professional-grade figures. Streamlines the 'PICRUSt2' analysis and visualization process. For more details, see Yang et al. (2023) <doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470>.
170                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Enables users to create simple plots of biological culture plates as well as microplates. Both continuous and discrete values can be plotted onto the plate layout. 
171                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            \n  Currently provides geom_balance_of_trade(), a 'ggplot2' layer that fills the area  \n  between exports and imports series (with automatic crossing detection  \n  and conditional coloring for surplus vs. deficit), and overlays lines  \n  and points by default.
172                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           \n    Provides the ggplot binning layer stat_summaries_hex(),\n    which functions similar to its singular form,\n    but allows the use of multiple statistics per bin.\n    Those statistics can be mapped to multiple bin aesthetics.
173                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A system for 'declaratively' creating graphics, based on "The\n    Grammar of Graphics". You provide the data, tell 'ggplot2' how to map\n    variables to aesthetics, what graphical primitives to use, and it\n    takes care of the details.
174                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Selected utilities, in particular 'geoms' and 'stats'\n    functions, extending the 'ggplot2' package. This package imports\n    functions from 'EnvStats' <doi:10.1007/978-1-4614-8456-1> by Millard\n    (2013), 'ggpp' <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggpp> by Aphalo et\n    al. (2023) and 'ggstats' <doi:10.5281/zenodo.10183964> by Larmarange\n    (2023), and then exports them. This package also contains modified\n    code from 'ggquickeda' <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggquickeda>\n    by Mouksassi et al. (2023) for Kaplan-Meier lines and ticks additions\n    to plots.  All functions are tested to make sure that they work\n    reliably.
175                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   A dataset about movies. This was previously contained in ggplot2,\n   but has been moved its own package to reduce the download size of ggplot2.
176                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            An 'RStudio' addin for teaching and learning making plot using the 'ggplot2' package.\n    You can learn each steps of making plot by clicking your mouse without coding.\n    You can get resultant code for the plot.
177                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Easily explore data by creating ggplots through a (shiny-)GUI. R-code to recreate graph provided.   
178                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Convert plot function call (using expression or formula) to 'grob' or 'ggplot' object that compatible to the 'grid' and 'ggplot2' ecosystem. With this package, we are able to e.g. using 'cowplot' to align plots produced by 'base' graphics, 'ComplexHeatmap', 'eulerr', 'grid', 'lattice', 'magick', 'pheatmap', 'vcd' etc. by converting them to 'ggplot' objects.
179                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Extensions to 'ggplot2' respecting the grammar of graphics\n    paradigm. Statistics to locate and tag peaks and valleys and to label plots\n    with the equation of a fitted polynomial model by ordinary least squares,\n    major axis, quantile and robust and resistant regression approaches. Line \n    and model equation for Normal mixture models. Labels for P-value, \n    R^2 or adjusted R^2 or information criteria for fitted models; parametric\n    and non-parametric correlation; ANOVA table or summary table for fitted \n    models as plot insets; annotations for multiple pairwise\n    comparisons with adjusted P-values. Model fit classes for which suitable \n    methods are provided by package 'broom' and 'broom.mixed' are supported as \n    well as user-defined wrappers on model fit functions, allowing model\n    selection and conditional labelling. Scales and stats to \n    build volcano and quadrant plots based on\n    outcomes, fold changes, p-values and false discovery rates.
180                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 At Novartis, we aimed at standardizing the set of diagnostic plots used for modeling\n  activities in order to reduce the overall effort required for generating such plots.\n  For this, we developed a guidance that proposes an adequate set of diagnostics and a toolbox,\n  called 'ggPMX' to execute them. 'ggPMX' is a toolbox that can generate all diagnostic plots at a quality sufficient\n  for publication and submissions using few lines of code. This package focuses on plots recommended by ISoP\n  <doi:10.1002/psp4.12161>. While not required, you can get/install the 'R' 'lixoftConnectors'\n    package in the 'Monolix' installation, as described at the following url\n    <https://monolixsuite.slp-software.com/r-functions/2024R1/installation-and-initialization>.\n    When 'lixoftConnectors' is available, 'R' can use 'Monolix' directly to create the required\n    Chart Data instead of exporting it from the 'Monolix' gui.
181                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A cross between a 2D density plot and a scatter plot,\n    implemented as a 'ggplot2' geom. Points in the scatter plot are \n    colored by the number of neighboring points. This is useful to\n    visualize the 2D-distribution of points in case of overplotting.
182                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A collection of layers for 'ggplot2'. Provides geoms built on\n    linear and radial gradients from the 'grid' package, giving areas, bars,\n    paths, rectangles, and ridgelines a fading or glowing visual effect.\n    Also includes mathematically driven layers — catenary curves, \n    Chaikin's corner-cutting smoothing\n    (Chaikin, 1974, <doi:10.1016/0146-664X(74)90028-8>), and Fourier-series\n    reconstruction — plus Lexis diagrams, isotype bar charts.
183                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Provides basic graphing functions to fully demonstrate\n    point-to-point connections in a polar coordinate space.
184                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Tools for working with polygons with holes in 'ggplot2', with a\n    new 'geom' for drawing a 'polypath' applying the 'evenodd' or 'winding'\n    rules.
185                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Create engaging population and point plots charts in R. 'ggpop' allows users to represent population data and points proportionally using customizable icons, facilitating the creation of circular representative population charts as well as any point-plots.
186                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Extensions to 'ggplot2' respecting the grammar of graphics \n    paradigm. Geometries: geom_table(), geom_plot() and geom_grob() add insets to \n    plots using native data coordinates, while geom_table_npc(), geom_plot_npc()\n    and geom_grob_npc() do the same using "npc" coordinates through new \n    aesthetics "npcx" and "npcy". Statistics: select observations based on 2D \n    density. Positions: radial nudging away from a center point and nudging away\n    from a line or curve; combined stacking and nudging; combined dodging and\n    nudging.
187                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Provides various themes, palettes, and other functions\n    that are used to customise ggplots to look like they were made in 'GraphPad \n    Prism'. The 'Prism'-look is achieved with theme_prism() and \n    scale_fill|colour_prism(), axes can be changed with custom guides like \n    guide_prism_minor(), and significance indicators added with add_pvalue().
188                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The 'ggplot2' package is excellent and flexible for elegant data\n    visualization in R. However the default generated plots requires some formatting\n    before we can send them for publication. Furthermore, to customize a 'ggplot',\n    the syntax is opaque and this raises the level of difficulty for researchers\n    with no advanced R programming skills. 'ggpubr' provides some easy-to-use\n    functions for creating and customizing 'ggplot2'- based publication ready plots.
189                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Automatically performs desired statistical tests (e.g. wilcox.test(), t.test()) to compare between groups, \n    and adds the resulting p-values to the plot with an annotation bar.\n    Visualizing group differences are frequently performed by boxplots, bar plots, etc.\n    Statistical test results are often needed to be annotated on these plots. \n    This package provides a convenient function that works on 'ggplot2' objects, \n    performs the desired statistical test between groups of interest and annotates the test results on the plot.
190                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             A quantile-quantile plot can be used to compare a sample of p-values \n  to the uniform distribution.  But when the dataset is big (i.e. > 1e4 p-values),\n  plotting the quantile-quantile plot can be slow.  geom_QQ uses all the data to\n  calculate the quantiles, but thins it out in a way that focuses on points near zero \n  before plotting to speed up plotting and decrease file size, when vector graphics are stored.  
191                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Quickly and easily perform exploratory data analysis by uploading your\n     data as a 'csv' file. Start generating insights using 'ggplot2' plots and\n     'table1' tables with descriptive stats, all using an easy-to-use point and click \n     'Shiny' interface.
192                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        An extension of 'ggplot2' to provide quiver plots to visualise vector fields. \n    This functionality is implemented using a geom to produce a new graphical layer, which\n    allows aesthetic options. This layer can be overlaid on a map to improve visualisation\n    of mapped data.
193                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Extend 'ggplot2' facets to panel layouts arranged in a grid\n    with ragged edges. facet_ragged_rows() groups panels into rows that\n    can vary in length, facet_ragged_cols() does the same but for columns.\n    These can be useful, for example, to represent nested or partially\n    crossed relationships between faceting variables.
194                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               The 'geom_rain()' function adds different geoms together using 'ggplot2' to create raincloud plots. 
195                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Graphic elements for exploring Random Forests using the\n    'randomForest' or 'randomForestSRC' package for survival, regression\n    and classification forests and 'ggplot2' package plotting. Implements\n    visualisations of the methods described in Breiman (2001)\n    <doi:10.1023/A:1010933404324> and Ishwaran, Kogalur, Blackstone, and\n    Lauer (2008) <doi:10.1214/08-AOAS169>.
