196                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             The grammar of graphics as implemented in ggplot2 is a poor fit for\n    graph and network visualizations due to its reliance on tabular data input.\n    ggraph is an extension of the ggplot2 API tailored to graph visualizations\n    and provides the same flexible approach to building up plots layer by layer.
197                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Intended for both technical and non-technical users to create\n    interactive data visualizations through a web browser GUI without writing any\n    code.
198                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Rasterize only specific layers of a 'ggplot2' plot while simultaneously keeping all labels and text in vector format. This allows users to keep plots within the reasonable size limit without loosing vector properties of the scale-sensitive information. 
199                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 You can use this function to easily draw a combined histogram and restricted cubic spline. \n    The function draws the graph through 'ggplot2'. RCS fitting requires the use of the rcs() function of the 'rms' package. \n    Can fit cox regression, logistic regression. This method was described by Per Kragh (2003) <doi:10.1002/sim.1497>.
200                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A collection of custom 'ggplot2'-based visualizations for \n    data exploration and analysis. Each function handles data \n    preprocessing and returns a object that can be further customized\n    using standard 'ggplot2' syntax.
201                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Provides 'ggplot2' extensions for political map making. Implements\n    new geometries for groups of simple feature geometries. Adds palettes and scales\n    for red to blue color mapping and for discrete maps. Implements tools for easy\n    label generation and placement, automatic map coloring, and themes.
202                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Complete themes for publication-quality 'ggplot2' visualisation. \n    Also provides functions to modify these based on the positional axis scales \n    and focus of a particular plot. 
203                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Provides text and label geoms for 'ggplot2' that help to avoid\n    overlapping text labels. Labels repel away from each other and away from the\n    data points.
204                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Provides functions that make it easy to reveal 'ggplot2' graphs incrementally. The functions take a plot produced with 'ggplot2' and return a list of plots showing data incrementally by panels, layers, groups, the values in an axis or any arbitrary aesthetic.
205                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Ridgeline plots provide a convenient way of visualizing changes in distributions over time or space. This package enables the creation of such plots in 'ggplot2'.
206                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             The risk plot may be one of the most commonly used figures in \n    tumor genetic data analysis. We can conclude the following two points: \n    Comparing the prediction results of the model with the real survival situation \n    to see whether the survival rate of the high-risk group is lower than that of the \n    low-level group, and whether the survival time of the high-risk group is \n    shorter than that of the low-risk group. The other is to compare the heat \n    map and scatter plot to see the correlation between the predictors and the \n    outcome.
207                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Creates bar plots with rounded corners using 'ggplot2'.\n    The code in this package was adapted from a solution provided by \n    Stack Overflow user 'sthoch' in the following post\n    <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62176038/r-ggplot2-bar-chart-with-round-corners-on-top-of-bar>.
208                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Calculates additive and dominance genetic relationship matrices and their inverses, in matrix and tabular-sparse formats. It includes functions for checking and processing pedigree, calculating inbreeding coefficients (Meuwissen & Luo, 1992 <doi:10.1186/1297-9686-24-4-305>), as well as functions to calculate the matrix of genetic group contributions (Q), and adding those contributions to the genetic merit of animals (Quaas (1988) <doi:10.3168/jds.S0022-0302(88)79691-5>). Calculation of Q is computationally extensive. There are computationally optimized functions to calculate Q.
209                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Works with 'ggplot2' to add a Van Gogh color palette to the user’s repertoire.\n It also has a function that work alongside 'ggplot2' to create more interesting data visualizations and add contextual information to the user’s plots.
210                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Sankey and alluvial diagrams visualise flows of quantities across\n    stages in stacked bars. This package makes it easy to create such\n    diagrams using 'ggplot2'.
211                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               The function combines a scatter plot with ridgelines to better visualise the distribution between sample groups. The plot is created with 'ggplot2'.
212                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Provides specialized visualization tools for Single-Case Experimental Design (SCED) \n    research using 'ggplot2'. SCED studies are a crucial methodology in behavioral and \n    educational research where individual participants serve as their own controls through \n    carefully designed experimental phases. This package extends 'ggplot2' to create \n    publication-ready graphics with professional phase change lines, support for multiple \n    baseline designs, and styling functions that follow SCED visualization conventions. \n    Key functions include adding phase change demarcation lines to existing plots and \n    formatting axes with broken axis appearance commonly used in single-case research.
213                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   A collection of 'ggplot2' color palettes inspired by\n    plots in scientific journals, data visualization libraries,\n    science fiction movies, and TV shows.
214                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Decision curve analysis is a method for evaluating and comparing prediction models that incorporates clinical consequences, requires only the data set on which the models are tested, and can be applied to models that have either continuous or dichotomous results. The 'ggscidca' package adds coloured bars of discriminant relevance to the traditional decision curve. Improved practicality and aesthetics. This method was described by Balachandran VP (2015) <doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(14)71116-7>.
215                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Annotation helper functions for publication-quality 'ggplot2' \n    visualisation. These functions make it easier to annotate plots in \n    a way that stays consistent with the set theme.
216                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Provides a 'ggplot2' geom and position for visualizing brain\n    region data on cortical, subcortical, and white matter tract atlases.\n    Brain atlas geometries are stored as simple features ('sf'), enabling\n    seamless integration with the 'ggplot2' ecosystem including faceting,\n    custom scales, and themes.  Mowinckel & Vidal-Piñeiro (2020)\n    <doi:10.1177/2515245920928009>.
217                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Provides the 'ggseg_atlas' S3 class used across the 'ggseg'\n    ecosystem for 2D and 3D brain visualisation. Ships three bundled atlases\n    ('Desikan-Killiany', 'FreeSurfer' 'aseg', 'TRACULA') and functions for\n    querying, subsetting, renaming, and enriching atlas objects. Also includes\n    readers for 'FreeSurfer' statistics files.
218                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Provides additional brain surface meshes for cortical and\n    cerebellar visualisation in the 'ggsegverse' ecosystem. Cortical surfaces\n    include pial, white, midthickness, semi-inflated, sphere, smoothwm, and\n    orig at fsaverage5 resolution. Cerebellar surfaces include the Spatially\n    Unbiased Infratentorial Template (SUIT) flatmap. All meshes follow the\n    same vertices/faces data frame format used by 'ggseg.formats' and\n    'ggseg3d'.
219                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Plot brain atlases as interactive 3D meshes using 'Three.js'\n    via 'htmlwidgets', or render publication-quality static images through\n    'rgl' and 'rayshader'. A pipe-friendly API lets you map data onto\n    brain regions, control camera angles, toggle region edges, overlay\n    glass brains, and snapshot or ray-trace the result. Additional\n    atlases are available through the 'ggsegverse' r-universe. Mowinckel\n    & Vidal-Piñeiro (2020) <doi:10.1177/2515245920928009>.
220                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             It provides a better alternative for stacked bar plot by creating a segmented total bar plot with custom annotations and labels. It is useful for visualizing the total of a variable and its segments in a single bar, making it easier to compare the segments and their contributions to the total.
221                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Provides an interactive workflow for visualizing structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group path diagrams, and network diagrams in R. Users can directly manipulate nodes and edges to create publication-quality figures while maintaining statistical model integrity. Supports integration with 'lavaan', 'OpenMx', 'tidySEM', and 'blavaan' etc. Features include parameter-based aesthetic mapping, generative AI assistance, and complete reproducibility by exporting metadata for script-based workflows. 
222                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The extensive range of functions provided by this package makes it possible to draw highly versatile sequence logos. Features include, but not limited to, modifying colour schemes and fonts used to draw the logo, generating multiple logo plots, and aiding the visualisation with annotations. Sequence logos can easily be combined with other plots 'ggplot2' plots.
223                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A set of wrapper functions that mainly re-produces most of the \n  sequence plots rendered with TraMineR::seqplot(). Whereas 'TraMineR' uses base \n  R to produce the plots this library draws on 'ggplot2'. \n  The plots are produced on the basis of a sequence object defined  \n  with TraMineR::seqdef(). The package automates the reshaping and plotting \n  of sequence data. Resulting plots are of class 'ggplot', i.e. components \n  can be added and tweaked using '+' and regular 'ggplot2' functions. 
224                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A collection of Geoms for R's 'ggplot2' library. geom_shadowpath(), geom_shadowline(), \n    geom_shadowstep() and geom_shadowpoint() functions draw a shadow below lines to make busy plots more \n    aesthetically pleasing. geom_glowpath(), geom_glowline(), geom_glowstep() and geom_glowpoint() add a \n    neon glow around lines to get a steampunk style.
225                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     The grammar of graphics as shown in 'ggplot2' has provided\n  an expressive API for users to build plots. 'ggside' extends 'ggplot2'\n  by allowing users to add graphical information about one of the main panel's\n  axis using a familiar 'ggplot2' style API with tidy data. This package is\n  particularly useful for visualizing metadata on a discrete axis, or summary\n  graphics on a continuous axis such as a boxplot or a density distribution.
226                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Enrich your 'ggplots' with group-wise comparisons.\n    This package provides an easy way to indicate if two groups are\n    significantly different. Commonly this is shown by a bracket on top\n    connecting the groups of interest which itself is annotated with the\n    level of significance (NS, *, **, ***).  The package provides a single\n    layer (geom_signif()) that takes the groups for comparison and the\n    test (t.test(), wilcox.text() etc.) as arguments and adds the\n    annotation to the plot.
227                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Provides 'ggplot2' extensions for creating skewed boxplots\n    using several statistical methods (Kimber, 1990 <doi:10.2307/2347808>; Hubert and Vandervieren, 2008 <doi:10.1016/j.csda.2007.11.008>; Adil et al., 2015 <doi:10.18187/pjsor.v11i1.500>; Babura et al., 2017 <doi:10.1063/1.4982872>; Walker et al., 2018 <doi:10.1080/00031305.2018.1448891>). The package implements custom\n    statistical transformations and geometries to visualize data\n    distributions with an emphasis on skewness.
228                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Simple tools to draw sky maps in 'ggplot2' using galactic or\n    equatorial coordinates. Includes custom coordinate systems, grid\n    labels, and helpers for sky map breaks.
229                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Functions for plotting, and animating, the output of importance samplers, sequential Monte Carlo samplers (SMC) and ensemble-based methods. The package can be used to plot and animate histograms, densities, scatter plots and time series, and to plot the genealogy of an SMC or ensemble-based algorithm. These functions all rely on algorithm output to be supplied in tidy format. A function is provided to transform algorithm output from matrix format (one Monte Carlo point per row) to the tidy format required by the plotting and animating functions.
230                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The 'ggplot2' package provides a powerful set of tools\n  for visualising and investigating data. The 'ggsoccer' package provides a\n  set of functions for elegantly displaying and exploring soccer event data\n  with 'ggplot2'. Providing extensible layers and themes, it is designed to\n  work smoothly with a variety of popular sports data providers.
231                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  An implementation of 'ggplot2'-methods to present the composition of Solvency II Solvency Capital Requirement (SCR) as a series of concentric circle-parts. \n Solvency II (Solvency 2) is European insurance legislation, coming in force by the delegated acts of October 10, 2014.\n <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ%3AL%3A2015%3A012%3ATOC>. \n Additional files, defining the structure of the Standard Formula (SF) method of the SCR-calculation are provided.\n The structure files can be adopted for localization or for insurance companies who use Internal Models (IM).\n Options are available for combining smaller components, horizontal and vertical scaling, rotation, and plotting only some circle-parts.\n With outlines and connectors several SCR-compositions can be compared, for example in ORSA-scenarios (Own Risk and Solvency Assessment).
232                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The aim of this package is to offer more variability of graphics based on the self-organizing maps.
233                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Functions to help with creating sparklines in the style of Edward Tufte <https://www.edwardtufte.com/bboard/q-and-a-fetch-msg?msg_id=0001OR&topic_id=1> in 'ggplot2'. It computes ribbon geoms with the interquartile ranges and points and/or labels at the beginning, end, max, and min points.
234                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Spatial data plus the power of the ggplot2 framework means easier mapping when input \n  data are already in the form of spatial objects.
235                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Additional annotations, stats, geoms and scales for plotting \n    "light" spectra with 'ggplot2', together with specializations of ggplot()\n    and autoplot() methods for spectral data and waveband definitions\n    stored in objects of classes defined in package 'photobiology'. Part of the \n    'r4photobiology' suite, Aphalo P. J. (2015) <doi:10.19232/uv4pb.2015.1.14>.
236                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 \n  Easily create overlapping grammar of graphics plots for scientific data visualization. \n  This style of plotting is particularly common in climatology and oceanography research communities.
237                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        A 'ggplot2' extension that provides flipped components:\n    horizontal versions of 'Stats' and 'Geoms', and vertical versions\n    of 'Positions'. This package is now superseded by 'ggplot2' itself\n    which now has full native support for horizontal layouts. It\n    remains available for backward compatibility.
238                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              To create the multiple polygonal point layer for easily discernible shapes, \n             we developed the package, it is like the 'geom_point' of 'ggplot2'.\n             It can be used to draw the scatter plot.
239                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Provides new statistics, new geometries and new positions for \n    'ggplot2' and a suite of functions to facilitate the creation of \n    statistical plots.
240                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Extension of 'ggplot2', 'ggstatsplot' creates graphics with\n    details from statistical tests included in the plots themselves. It\n    provides an easier syntax to generate information-rich plots for\n    statistical analysis of continuous (violin plots, scatterplots,\n    histograms, dot plots, dot-and-whisker plots) or categorical (pie and\n    bar charts) data. Currently, it supports the most common types of\n    statistical approaches and tests: parametric, nonparametric, robust,\n    and Bayesian versions of t-test/ANOVA, correlation analyses,\n    contingency table analysis, meta-analysis, and regression analyses.\n    References: Patil (2021) <doi:10.21105/joss.03236>.
241                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Provides an extension to 'ggplot2'\n  (Wickham, 2016, <doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4>) for creating two types of\n  continuous confidence interval plots (Violin CI and Gradient CI plots),\n  typically for the sample mean. These plots contain multiple user-defined\n  confidence areas with varying colours, defined by the underlying\n  t-distribution used to compute standard confidence intervals for the mean of\n  the normal distribution when the variance is unknown. Two types of plots are\n  available, a gradient plot with rectangular areas, and a violin plot where\n  the shape (horizontal width) is defined by the probability density function\n  of the t-distribution. These visualizations are studied in\n  (Helske, Helske, Cooper, Ynnerman, and Besancon, 2021) \n  <doi:10.1109/TVCG.2021.3073466>.
242                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Create epicurves, epigantt charts, and diverging bar charts\n    using 'ggplot2'. Prepare data for visualisation or other reporting for\n    infectious disease surveillance and outbreak investigation (time\n    series data).  Includes tidy functions to solve date based\n    transformations for common reporting tasks, like (A) seasonal date\n    alignment for respiratory disease surveillance, (B) date-based case\n    binning based on specified time intervals like isoweek, epiweek, month\n    and more, (C) automated detection and marking of the new year based on\n    the date/datetime axis of the 'ggplot2', (D) labelling of the last\n    value of a time-series.  An introduction on how to use epicurves can\n    be found on the US CDC website (2012,\n    <https://www.cdc.gov/training/quicklearns/epimode/index.html>).
243                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Functions for survey data including svydesign objects from the 'survey' package that call 'ggplot2' to make bar charts, histograms, boxplots, and hexplots of survey data.
