244                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Ease the creation of time-to-event (i.e. survival) endpoint\n    figures. The modular functions create figures ready for publication.\n    Each of the functions that add to or modify the figure are written as\n    proper 'ggplot2' geoms or stat methods, allowing the functions from\n    this package to be combined with any function or customization from\n    'ggplot2' and other 'ggplot2' extension packages.

246                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Extends the 'ggplot2' plotting system to support network visualization. Inspired by the 'Method 1' in 'ggtree' (G Yu (2018) <doi:10.1093/molbev/msy194>), 'ggtangle' is designed to work with network associated data. 
247                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A collection of palettes and themes for 'ggplot2', offering a light, pastel aesthetic. Syntax follows the 'viridis' package. 
248                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Extends the functionality of 'ggplot2', providing the capability\n    to plot ternary diagrams for (subset of) the 'ggplot2' geometries. 249                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     A 'ggplot2' extension that enables the rendering of\n    complex formatted plot labels (titles, subtitles, facet labels,\n    axis labels, etc.). Text boxes with automatic word wrap are also\n    supported.
250                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Rstudio add-in that delivers a graphical interface for editing 'ggplot2' theme elements.
251                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Some extra themes, geoms, and scales for 'ggplot2'.\n    Provides 'ggplot2' themes and scales that replicate the look of plots\n    by Edward Tufte, Stephen Few, 'Fivethirtyeight', 'The Economist', 'Stata',\n    'Excel', and 'The Wall Street Journal', among others.\n    Provides 'geoms' for Tufte's box plot and range frame.
252                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Designed to customize 'ggplot' graphics according to the institutional identity of the University of Ljubljana. 
253                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           \n  Create tibbles and lists of 'ggplot' figures that can be modified as easily as\n  regular 'ggplot' figures. 254                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Annotation of 'ggplot2' plots with arbitrary 'TikZ' code, using absolute data or relative plot coordinates.
255                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Extends the capabilities of 'ggplot2' by providing grammatical\n    elements and plot helpers designed for visualizing temporal patterns. The \n    package implements a grammar of temporal graphics, which leverages calendar\n    structures to highlight changes over time. The package also provides plot \n    helper functions to quickly produce commonly used time series graphics,\n    including time plots, season plots, and seasonal sub-series plots.
256                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Provides 'ggplot2' geoms that allow groups of data points to be\n    outlined or highlighted for emphasis. This is particularly useful when\n    working with dense datasets that are prone to overplotting.
257                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Provides a simple way to translate text elements in 'ggplot2' plots using a dictionary-based approach.
258                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Provides 'ggplot2' geoms analogous to 'geom_col()' and 'geom_bar()'\n    that allow for treemaps using 'treemapify' nested within each bar segment.\n    Also provides geometries for subgroup bordering and text annotation.
259                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Add trendline and confidence interval of linear or nonlinear regression model and\n    show equation to 'ggplot' as simple as possible. For a general overview of the methods used in\n\t  this package, see Ritz and Streibig (2008) <doi:10.1007/978-0-387-09616-2> and \n\t  Greenwell and Schubert Kabban (2014) <doi:10.32614/RJ-2014-009>.
260                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     A collection of several geoms to create graphics, using\n    'ggplot2' and the Cartesian coordinate system. You use the familiar\n    mapping 'Grammar of Graphics' without the need to do another\n    transformation into polar coordinates.
261                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Replace the standard x-axis in 'ggplots' with a combination matrix\n  to visualize complex set overlaps. 'UpSet' has introduced a new way to visualize\n  the overlap of sets as an alternative to Venn diagrams. \n  This package provides a simple way to produce such plots using 'ggplot2'. \n  In addition it can convert any categorical axis into a combination\n  matrix axis.
262                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A simple, opinionated toolkit for visualizing genomic variant data\n    using a 'ggplot2'-native grammar. Accepts VCF files or plain data frames and\n    produces publication-ready lollipop plots, consequence summaries, mutational\n    spectrum charts, and cohort-level comparisons with minimal code. Designed for\n    both wet-lab biologists and experienced bioinformaticians.
263                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Functions to produce 'ggplot2'-based plots of objects produced by\n    functions in the 'vegan' package. Provides 'fortify()', 'autoplot()', and\n    'tidy()' methods for many of 'vegan''s functions. The aim of 'ggvegan' is to\n    make it easier to work within the 'tidyverse' with 'vegan'.
264                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          An easy-to-use way to draw pretty Venn diagrams using 'ggplot2'.\n    This package provides functions to create Venn diagrams with customizable\n    colors, labels, and styling options.
265                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Easy-to-use functions to generate 2-7 sets Venn or upset plot in publication quality. \n  'ggVennDiagram' plot Venn or upset using well-defined geometry dataset and 'ggplot2'. The shapes of 2-4 sets \n  Venn use circles and ellipses, while the shapes of 4-7 sets Venn use irregular polygons (4 has both forms), which \n  are developed and imported from another package 'venn', authored by Adrian Dusa. We provided internal functions to \n  integrate shape data with user provided sets data, and calculated the geometry of every regions/intersections \n  of them, then separately plot Venn in four components, set edges/labels, and region edges/labels.\n  From version 1.0, it is possible to customize these components as you demand in ordinary 'ggplot2' grammar.\n  From version 1.4.4, it supports unlimited number of sets, as it can draw a plain upset plot automatically when\n  number of sets is more than 7.

Tremblay y Julian Hernandez-Serrano. Incluye datos\n    de ecologia, salud publica, educacion, economia y biodiversidad\n    para la ensenanza de visualizacion de datos con 'ggplot2'.
267                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       A 'ggplot2' extension for visualizing vector fields in two-dimensional \n           space. Provides flexible tools for creating vector and stream field layers, \n           visualizing gradients and potential fields, and smoothing vector and \n           scalar data to estimate underlying patterns. 
268                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Preview what a 'ggplot2' plot would look like if you save it to a file. \n    Attach picture dimensions as a canvas() element and get an instant preview. \n    These dimensions will then be used when you save the plot.
269                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                An implementation of an interactive grammar of graphics,\n    taking the best parts of 'ggplot2', combining them with the reactive\n    framework of 'shiny' and drawing web graphics using 'vega'.
270                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Provides functionality to create customizable volcano plots for\n    visualizing differential gene expression analysis results. The package\n    offers options to highlight genes of interest, adjust significance\n    thresholds, customize colors, and add informative labels. Designed\n    specifically for RNA-seq data analysis workflows.
271                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Provides publication-ready volcano plots for visualizing differential expression results, commonly used in RNA-seq and similar analyses. This tool helps create high-quality visual representations of data using the 'ggplot2' framework Wickham (2016) <doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4>.
272                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Provides browser-native 'WebGL' rendering for R graphics through\n    'htmlwidgets'. The package supports grammar-style graphics workflows and\n    renderer-ready specifications for dense analytical and scientific scenes,\n    including point, line, trajectory, raster, vector, mesh, and surface\n    layers, shader-driven display modes, timeline controls, structured views,\n    selection metadata, and publication-oriented static export helpers.\n    Rendering stays in the browser, and the core package remains\n    cross-platform without requiring 'CUDA', 'Metal', or 'OpenCL' toolchains.
273                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Width helper functions for publication-quality 'ggplot2' \n    visualisation. These functions make it easier to create geoms such \n    as bars that have a consistent width appearance across plots.
274                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Provides a word cloud text geom for 'ggplot2'. Texts\n    are placed so that they do not overlap as in 'ggrepel'.  The algorithm\n    used is a variation around the one of 'wordcloud2.js'.
275                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           The 'ggplot2' package is the state-of-the-art toolbox for creating and formatting graphs. However, it is easy to forget how certain formatting commands are named and sometimes users find themselves asking: How do you rotate the x-axis labels again? Or how do you hide the legend...? This package allows users to issue natural language commands related to theme-related styling of plots (colors, font size and such), which then are translated into valid 'ggplot2' commands.
276                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A Gibbs sampler corresponding to a Group \n    Inverse-Gamma Gamma (GIGG) regression model with adjustment covariates. \n    Hyperparameters in the GIGG prior specification can either be fixed by the \n    user or can be estimated via Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation.\n    Jonathan Boss, Jyotishka Datta, Xin Wang, Sung Kyun Park, Jian Kang, Bhramar \n    Mukherjee (2021) <arXiv:2102.10670>.
277                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             All the data and functions used to produce the book. We do not expect\n    most people to use the package for any other reason than to get simple access to the\n    'JAGS' model files, the data, and perhaps run some of the simple examples.\n    The authors of the book are David Lucy (now sadly deceased) and James Curran. It is \n    anticipated that a manuscript will be provided to Taylor and Francis around February 2020, with\n    bibliographic details to follow at that point. Until such time, further information\n    can be obtained by emailing James Curran.
278                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Provides smooth approximations to the L0 norm penalty for\n    estimating sparse Gaussian graphical models (GGMs). Network estimation\n    is performed using the Local Linear Approximation (LLA) framework\n    (Fan & Li, 2001 <doi:10.1198/016214501753382273>;\n    Zou & Li, 2008 <doi:10.1214/009053607000000802>) with five penalty\n    functions: arctangent (Wang & Zhu, 2016 <doi:10.1155/2016/6495417>),\n    EXP (Wang, Fan, & Zhu, 2018 <doi:10.1007/s10463-016-0588-3>), Gumbel,\n    Log (Candes, Wakin, & Boyd, 2008 <doi:10.1007/s00041-008-9045-x>),\n    and Weibull. Adaptive penalty parameters for EXP, Gumbel, and Weibull\n    are estimated via maximum likelihood, and model selection uses\n    information criteria including AIC, BIC, and EBIC (Extended BIC).\n    Simulation functions generate multivariate normal data from GGMs with\n    stochastic block model or small-world (Watts-Strogatz) network structures.
279                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Provides classes and methods for objects, whose indexing\n      naturally starts from zero. Subsetting, indexing and mathematical\n      operations are defined naturally between lagged objects and lagged\n      and base R objects. Recycling is not used, except for singletons.\n      The single bracket operator doesn't drop dimensions by default.
280                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Helps to render interlinear glossed linguistic examples in html \n    'rmarkdown' documents and then semi-automatically compiles the list of\n    glosses at the end of the document. It also provides a database of linguistic\n    glosses.
281                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Inspired by the the 'futile.logger' R package and 'logging'\n    Python module, this utility provides a flexible and extensible way of\n    formatting and delivering log messages with low overhead.
282                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Pure R implementation of the ubiquitous log4j package. It offers hierarchic \n  loggers, multiple handlers per logger, level based filtering, space handling in messages \n  and custom formatting.
283                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         \n    An effortless 'ndjson' (newline-delimited 'JSON') logger, with two primary\n    log-writing interfaces. It provides a set of wrappings for base R's\n    message(), warning(), and stop() functions that maintain identical\n    functionality, but also log the handler message to an 'ndjson' log file.\n    'loggit' also exports its internal 'loggit()' function for powerful and\n    configurable custom logging. No change in existing code is necessary to use\n    this package, and should only require additions to fully leverage the power\n    of the logging system. 'loggit' also provides a log reader for reading an\n    'ndjson' log file into a data frame, log rotation, and live echo of the\n    'ndjson' log messages to terminal 'stdout' for log capture by external\n    systems (like containers). 'loggit' is ideal for Shiny apps, data pipelines,\n    modeling work flows, and more. Please see the vignettes for detailed example\n    use cases.
284                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \n    An easy-to-use 'ndjson' (newline-delimited 'JSON') logger.\n    It provides a set of wrappers for base R's message(), warning(), and\n    stop() functions that maintain identical functionality, but also log\n    the handler message to an 'ndjson' log file.\n    No change in existing code is necessary to use this package, \n    and only a few additional adjustments are needed to fully \n    utilize its potential.
285                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Provides a bridge between the 'loon' and  'ggplot2' packages.  Extends the grammar of ggplot to add clauses to create interactive 'loon' plots. Existing ggplot(s) can be turned into interactive 'loon' plots and 'loon' plots into static ggplot(s); the function 'loon.ggplot()' is the bridge from one plot structure to the other.
286                                                                                              \n    According to a phenomenon known as "the wisdom of the crowds," \n    combining point estimates from multiple judges often provides a \n    more accurate aggregate estimate than using a point estimate from\n    a single judge. However, if the judges use shared information in \n    their estimates, the simple average will over-emphasize this common\n    component at the expense of the judges’ private information. \n    Asa Palley & Ville Satopää (2021) "Boosting the Wisdom of Crowds\n    Within a Single Judgment Problem: Selective Averaging Based on Peer Predictions"\n    <https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Papers.cfm?abstract_id=3504286> proposes\n    a procedure for calculating a weighted average of the judges’ individual\n    estimates such that resulting aggregate estimate appropriately combines\n    the judges' collective information within a single estimation problem. \n    The authors use both simulation and data from six experimental studies\n    to illustrate that the weighting procedure outperforms existing averaging-like\n    methods, such as the equally weighted average, trimmed average, and median.\n    This aggregate estimate -- know as "the knowledge-weighted estimate" --\n    inputs a) judges' estimates of a continuous outcome (E) and \n    b) predictions of others' average estimate of this outcome (P).  \n    In this R-package, the function knowledge_weighted_estimate(E,P) \n    implements the knowledge-weighted estimate. Its use is illustrated\n    with a simple stylized example and on real-world experimental data. 
287                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Distance between multivariate generalised Gaussian distributions, as presented by N. Bouhlel and A. Dziri (2019) <doi:10.1109/LSP.2019.2915000>. Manipulation of multivariate generalised Gaussian distributions (methods presented by Gomez, Gomez-Villegas and Marin (1998) <doi:10.1080/03610929808832115> and Pascal, Bombrun, Tourneret and Berthoumieu (2013) <doi:10.1109/TSP.2013.2282909>).
288                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      \n    MHCnuggets (<https://github.com/KarchinLab/mhcnuggets>) is a Python\n    tool to predict MHC class I and MHC class II epitopes.\n    This package allows one to call MHCnuggets from R.
289                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Aggregates matrix population models (MPMs) in both the lambda (stable \n    growth rate) and R0 (net reproductive rate) frameworks, including standard and \n    elasticity-consistent aggregators. Standard aggregation in the lambda framework \n    maintains consistent lambda and stable stage distribution, while standard aggregation \n    in the R0 framework maintains consistent R0 and cohort stable stage distribution. \n    Elasticity-consistent aggregators maintain these same consistencies with respect\n    to the chosen framework and additionally preserve consistent reproductive values in \n    the lambda framework and cohort reproductive values in the R0 framework. Aggregation \n    can take the form of general-to-general MPM (mpm_aggregate) or Leslie-to-Leslie\n    MPM (leslie_aggregate).
290                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Wraps the 'nametag' library <https://github.com/ufal/nametag>, allowing users to find and extract entities (names, persons, locations, addresses, ...) in raw text and build your own entity recognition models.\n    Based on a maximum entropy Markov model which is described in Strakova J., Straka M. and Hajic J. (2013) <https://ufal.mff.cuni.cz/~straka/papers/2013-tsd_ner.pdf>.
291                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A framework for systematic exploration of\n    association rules  (Agrawal et al., 1994, <https://www.vldb.org/conf/1994/P487.PDF>), \n    contrast patterns  (Chen, 2022, <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2209.13556>),\n    emerging patterns  (Dong et al., 1999, <doi:10.1145/312129.312191>),\n    subgroup  discovery (Atzmueller, 2015, <doi:10.1002/widm.1144>),\n    and conditional correlations (Hájek, 1978,  <doi:10.1007/978-3-642-66943-9>).\n    User-defined functions may also be supplied to guide custom pattern searches.\n    Supports both crisp (Boolean) and fuzzy data. Generates candidate conditions\n    expressed as elementary conjunctions, evaluates them on a dataset, and\n    inspects the induced sub-data for statistical, logical, or structural\n    properties such as  associations, correlations, or contrasts. Includes methods \n    for visualization of logical structures and supports interactive exploration\n    through integrated Shiny applications. 
292                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Density, distribution function, quantile function and random generation for the Odd Log-Logistic Generalized Gamma proposed in Prataviera, F. et al (2017) <doi:10.1080/00949655.2016.1238088>.
293                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Performs outrigger local polynomial regression/ distributional adaptation, using a score-matching spline estimator of the conditional score function.\n    Details of the method can be found in Young, Shah and Samworth (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2603.11282>.
